chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim from Khalaf ibn Hammad from 'Umar ibn Aban who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever drinks the intoxicant, it is a right upon Allah, Exalted and Mighty, to make him drink from the mud of Khubal.' I said: 'And what is the mud of Khubal?' He said: 'The pus of the vulvas of the prostitutes.'

key_terms.طِينَةِ خَبَالٍ: Mud of Khubal (a specific impure substance)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Tinat Khubal' mentioned in the hadith about drinking intoxicants?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a specific divine retribution (*haqqan ala Allah*) for consumers of intoxicants, linking the spiritual impurity of *khamr* to a physical manifestation in the afterlife. The definition of 'mud of Khubal' as the pus of prostitutes (*sadiid furuj al-bagha'i*) serves as a symbolic mirror to the drinker, reflecting the moral corruption of the wine through the bodily fluids of promiscuity, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the correspondence between vice and its punishment.
